text:
maria: Heads up — ran a long-context soak (1.5M tokens, steady stream) against dedicated cluster and observed continuous KV memory growth. Heap doesn't reclaim; kvcache bytes monotonically increase ~200MB/hr. Suspect stale segments not being reclaimed after eviction/compaction.

kevin: Do you have a small repro and logs? which build/hash? :eyes:

maria: repro is a streaming chat loop hitting the same session id and appending tokens. Build: main@b3f9d2a. Logs excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-18T08:12:03Z] kvcache: append seg=0x7f88 size=4096 req_id=1245 offset=0 tag=0x1a2b
[2026-03-18T08:12:03Z] kvcache: append seg=0x7f90 size=4096 req_id=1246 offset=4096 tag=0x1a2b
[2026-03-18T08:12:03Z] kvcache: evict seg=0x7f88 tombstone=true next_offset=8192
[2026-03-18T08:12:03Z] kvcache: append seg=0x7fa0 size=4096 req_id=1271 offset=0 tag=0x1a2b
```
Note: after eviction we see new segment at offset 0 but later reads attempt to read at global offset 4096 and get shifted data.

sophie: hm that looks like request_id or global-offset slip. Could be the rotation/compaction path not translating request-scoped offsets to global offsets when tombstones are present.

rahul: we had a related bug where the slot rotation logic subtracted the wrong base when wraps happened. Reproducer I used was: make long prefix, force eviction by lowering cache size, then issue alternating requests with same session id. Command: 
```bash
./tools/kv_repro --session test-123 --tokens 1500000 --evict-at 256MB
```
That triggered stale reads for me.

perf-bot: nightly-kvflux job (main@b3f9d2a) flagged memory-leak-suspect for kvcache on dedicated-3. CI flamegraph links: (attached). Hot functions: kvcache::append, memmove, kv_segment::read_at. Token-level cost +7% compared to baseline.

kevin: Can you paste a minimal dump of the kvcache metadata (slot table)? we need to check segment stamps and request_id mapping.

maria: pasted anonymized slot dump: 
```
slots: [ {slot_id:42, seg=0x7f88, base_global=0, size=4096, tag=0x1a2b, last_req=1245}, {slot_id:43, seg=0x7f90, base_global=4096, size=4096, tag=0x1a2b, last_req=1246}, {slot_id:44, seg=0x7fa0, base_global=8192, size=4096, tag=0x1a2b, last_req=1271} ]
reads: request 1275 tried read global_offset=4096 -> resolved to seg=0x7fa0 offset=0 (wrong)
```
So lookup translated global_offset->seg incorrectly (overlapping base_global arithmetic).

sophie: That last line is the smoking gun. It means the compaction path updated base_global for newer segments but didn't adjust the mapping table used by the read path under concurrency. Race between compactor and reader.

rahul: I dug in — compaction uses a temp remap slice that is swapped under a spinlock, but the reader uses an rcu-ish fast path that reads without lock and relies on per-segment "stamp" to validate. If stamp check fails we should fallback, but fallback path has a bug: it compares stamp==0 as "invalid" but compaction sets stamp->0 transiently which looks invalid and causes a fast-path acceptance of stale mapping.

maria: added quick instrumentation to assert on mapping stability; reproduced locally. Fail trace: 
```
kvcache::read_at -> map_lookup() returned seg=0x7fa0 for global=4096
kv_segment::validate_stamp returned true (stamp transiently zero)
-> read returned data from new seg, but offset should have been from previous seg -> mismatch
```

kevin: Nice catch. Two suggested fixes: (1) make compaction set new stamp non-zero before swapping and never write zero; (2) make reader treat stamp==0 as "in-flight" and retry (not accept). We should do both defensively.

tilly: +1 on both. Also add a unit that races compaction with concurrent reads for 1000 iterations. I can add a flaky CI stress job.

maria: I prototyped change (option 1) in local branch main@fix/kv-stamp-order — with change memory stabilized during the 6h soak (no monotonic growth). Perf bot re-run shows token-cost back to baseline.

perf-bot: rerun results: memory-regression resolved, CPU tail-bound on memcpy reduced, token cost delta now +0.5% (within noise).

kevin: can you open a PR with the patch + the stress unit + a short integration test that simulates alternating session requests and forced eviction? assign to me and rahul for review. Add a note in CHANGES about compaction stamp ordering.

maria: will open PR in ~30m. Thanks all. :tada:

tilly: Also let's add brief postmortem to eng-runtime channel once PR merges so support can patch any private deployments that still run older runtime.

maria: good call. I will do that and include a small remediation script to force a safe restart for affected Dedicated nodes.

kevin: great work. tracking: #PR-8421, marking follow-up ticket ENG-RUN-1195 for backport to 2026-Q1 build.
